label: Quickstart: Model-as-a-Service on IBM Fusion
description: Deploy a complete Model-as-a-Service stack on IBM Fusion with Red Hat OpenShift AI: install OpenShift AI operators, wire up Fusion object storage, stand up a Model Registry, deploy GPU-backed inference with LLM-D, expose models through a secure gateway, and validate a live inference endpoint.

label: Quickstart: Namespace-as-a-Service on Fusion
description: Turn namespace provisioning into a self-service Developer Hub wizard backed by GitOps. Covers platform-team setup, GitHub auth, Helm values, and the ArgoCD naas-controller, plus the developer flow for requesting, resizing, and deleting namespaces, each auto-configured with resource quotas, network policies, and RBAC roles via a reviewable Pull Request.

label: Creating and building AI agents with watsonx Orchestrate ADK
description: Install the watsonx Orchestrate Agent Development Kit and build agents using either the conversational AI Builder or declarative YAML definitions, including tools, connections, and knowledge bases.

label: Deploying agents in watsonx Orchestrate
description: Release a working agent into production so users can access it, either through the watsonx Orchestrate UI or the ADK CLI.

label: Deploy watsonx.ai and watsonx Orchestrate on Fusion HCI
description: Use the Software Hub service on IBM Fusion HCI to automate prerequisites, storage class selection, and resource pre-checks before installing watsonx.ai and watsonx Orchestrate.

label: AI workloads on IBM Fusion HCI
description: How IBM Fusion HCI runs container and VM AI workloads on its GPU nodes, validated end-to-end with watsonx for consistent training and inference performance.

label: Registering models from the Model Catalog
description: Import and register foundation models from HuggingFace or the Red Hat model repository into the Model Registry, including versioning and metadata setup, before deployment.

label: GPU servers and sizing on Fusion HCI
description: Reference for available GPU server hardware, card counts, and capacity on Fusion HCI, used to size GPU nodes for MaaS inference workloads.

label: Prerequisite: Fusion Developer Hub via GitOps
description: Deploy Red Hat Developer Hub on Fusion using GitOps, required before enabling the NaaS or MaaS self-service templates.

label: Prerequisite: Fusion GitOps (ArgoCD) Quickstart
description: Install OpenShift GitOps/ArgoCD on your Fusion cluster, the reconciliation engine both the NaaS controller and other self-service templates depend on.
